subject: Re: Post-call recap & eval plan — model parity and acceptance thresholds
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@paygrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap & eval plan — model parity and acceptance thresholds

Hi Alex — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

What we heard (requirements):
- High precision on entity extraction and billing-code mapping (~F1 focus).
- Tight latency needs for customer-facing flows (<300ms p95 for single-turn inference).
- Data handling: PII redaction required in test corpus; we will use your sanitized export.

Recommended eval plan:
1) We run a 2-week model-fit eval against your sanitized prompt set (attached: paygrid-eval-prompt-set-v1.csv).
2) Models to include: open variants (Llama 2 70B quantized, Mistral-Instruct 34B, Falcon 180B-1.5) and a Redwood-calibrated variant that prioritizes latency (quantized 8-bit).
3) Acceptance thresholds:
   - F1 parity target: >= 0.95 of your proprietary baseline on the extraction prompts (if baseline F1 = 0.90, acceptance >= 0.855).
   - Latency: p95 <= 300ms for the optimized config.
   - Regression tolerance: no single prompt set should drop >5% absolute F1 vs baseline.

Deliverables we’ll share: detailed per-prompt metrics, confusion matrices, and a summary benchmark PDF (link included). If open models meet parity on quality and hit latency targets with quantization and batching, we can discuss pricing/operational choices and a pilot.

Next steps:
- Please confirm the sanitized dataset delivery timeline (you mentioned EOD Wed).
- If acceptable, I’ll kick off the eval and share interim results after 48 hours.

Attachments: paygrid-eval-prompt-set-v1.csv, mutual-action-plan-paygrid.docx

Best,
Lauren
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com
redwood.com

--
On Mon, 02 Nov 2026 at 14:05 Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@paygrid.com> wrote:
> Thanks Lauren — that was helpful. Sofia and I will get the sanitized export over by EOD Wednesday. Appreciate the clarity on thresholds.
> 
> Quick Q on acceptance: is the 5% absolute regression cap a hard stop or negotiable? We have some edge-case prompts where our in-house model is unusually strong.
> 
> - Alex

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@paygrid.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@paygrid.com>, procurement@paygrid.com
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 09:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & eval plan — model parity and acceptance thresholds

Lauren — thanks for the plan. We’ll send the sanitized export (CSV) by EOD Wednesday as discussed. A couple quick points: 

1) On acceptance thresholds: our baseline F1 is around 0.92 on the current extraction set. We want to be careful about broad-brush caps — a few edge-case prompts where our baseline scores much higher could be acceptable to miss if the overall user impact is low. Can you map per-prompt criticality?

2) On latency: our production SLA for customer-facing inference is 250ms p95. If Redwood can demonstrate consistent p95 <= 250ms on a dedicated instance (with the recommended quantized model), that’d be ideal — otherwise we need to scope the fallback behavior.

3) Procurement: looping in procurement for contract cadence/scope. We’ll want a clear mutual action plan and a 30-day pilot commitment.

If you want, we can have a short sync Thursday to finalize the acceptance criteria.

—Alex

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 04 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Post-call recap & eval plan — model parity and acceptance thresholds

Internal — forwarding Alex’s reply. Key asks:
- Map per-prompt criticality so we can weight the evaluation. Alex asked to allow some low-impact edge-case misses.
- Target latency tightened to 250ms p95 for the pilot (PayGrid ask).
- Procurement wants a 30-day pilot + MAP doc (I attached our mutual-action-plan-paygrid.docx and the prompt set).

Proposed internal plan:
- Run two parallel eval tracks: (A) quality-first (L2 70B quantized, Mistral 34B) with full prompt weighting; (B) latency-first (Redwood-optimized 8-bit variant on our Dedicated node) measuring p95 under a synthetic, PayGrid-like QPS.
- Define acceptance as: weighted F1 >= 0.95 * baseline AND per-critical-prompt drop <= 5% absolute; if some non-critical prompts drop 6-8% absolute we can flag but not fail the pilot.
- Deliver interim metrics at 48h and full report at 14 days.

Marissa — can you confirm the recommended model variants, quantization profile, and the synthetic load config (QPS/sequence length distribution) so I can confirm with Alex? Aditya — can you pre-seed the eval infra and ensure logs/tracing are enabled for per-prompt debugging?

Thanks,
Lauren

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Nov 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-call recap & eval plan — model parity and acceptance thresholds

Lauren / Aditya — plan looks good. Quick notes and technical asks: 

Model variants we recommend for the two tracks:
- Quality-first: Llama-2-70B-chat (8-bit quantized, tuned prompt templates), Mistral-Instruct-34B (fp16), fallback Falcon-180B-1.5 (quantized) for hard prompts.
- Latency-first: Redwood-optimized 70B 8-bit with KV cache priming + reduced context window for production-simulated runs.

Quantization/profile: start with dynamic 8-bit (q8_dynamic) for Llama and Falcon variants; Mistral we keep fp16 initially to check quality headroom. If memory allows, try q4f32 for a subset to measure quality vs latency trade-offs.

Synthetic load config (to hit PayGrid SLA target):
- QPS: 15-20 (burst to 50) to simulate peak commerce flows.
- Sequence lengths: 80-220 tokens (95th percentile ~200).
- Batch strategy: small-batch continuous batching with max-latency bound 40ms to protect p95.

Acceptance instrumentation: we’ll produce per-prompt deltas vs their baseline plus a weighted aggregate (weighting rubric TBD with Alex). Also recommend adding a small human eval of 150 randomly sampled failed/near-fail prompts to qualify user-impact.

Attachments: open-model-benchmarks-20261102.pdf (interim numbers from internal lab).

I’ll seed the infra today and run a quick 48h smoke to get initial delta matrix.

—Marissa
Principal Applied ML — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
